title: ContextSafe evaluation receipt document 0.3
$comment: Pre-1.0 shape of the contextsafe-receipt-v1.schema.json listed in docs/04-ARCHITECTURE.md section 8; the published payload is the iteration-4 claim-minimal payload, not a reviewed pilot receipt. 0.3 adds the B-031 first-observed-divergence section and the per-outcome evidence trace (A-034, A-035) and changes nothing that 0.2 carried; a 0.2 document differs in its payload schema_version and lacks both, so it does not validate here, by design. The document root carries the untrusted envelope, the deterministic payload, and the payload hash. #/$defs/deterministic_payload is the standalone contract for the hashed payload. JSON Schema validates structure only; ContextSafe tests additionally verify payload_sha256 agreement and enum parity with the runtime status, reason, checkpoint, concept, evidence-state, and divergence-status types.
x-contextsafe-semantic-constraints: payload_sha256 equals the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of payload
the pinned limitations bound this document only; F-030 also requires every rendered report derived from it to present each disclosure, which no JSON Schema can check
envelope fields are unauthenticated caller-declared metadata that never enter payload or payload_sha256
a divergence entry's at and after name observed checkpoints only; an unobserved checkpoint is never named there, and its state in the checkpoints list is the only thing said about it
a valid document proves structure and claim minimality only; it proves no signature, trusted time, clinical approval, or external validation

evidence_state.$comment: What the observation set held for one concept at one checkpoint. unobserved is the absence of evidence and nothing more: never agreement, never divergence, never blamed.

divergence_status.$comment: diverged and indeterminate are located at an observed checkpoint; agreed_where_observed says every observed checkpoint agreed and nothing about the unobserved ones; unobserved says there were too few observed checkpoints to compare.

structural_pointer.$comment: A source pointer is a structural path and nothing else, in one of the three dialects the readers emit, each over one closed vocabulary: the $-rooted path of the canonical case manifest, the canonical JSON evidence envelope and the LIS export readers ($ followed by one or more segments, each either .name from the vocabulary or [n] with n a non-negative integer without leading zeros); the RFC 6901 JSON Pointer the FHIR R4 reader emits, whose reference tokens are vocabulary names or indices, at most sixteen of them; and the HL7 v2 reader's $.SEG[n]-field.rep.comp, whose only word is a segment name, meaning one of the five vocabulary words shaped like one. This is the same vocabulary the runtime validator enforces on the observation set (contextsafe.validation.STRUCTURAL_POINTER_SEGMENTS), and the bounds are its bounds: maxLength is the smaller of MAX_STRING_LENGTH and SOURCE_POINTER_MAX_LENGTH, and the sixteen is JSON_POINTER_MAX_SEGMENTS. It said 160 until 2026-09-04, so a 129-character path of nothing but vocabulary words validated here and was refused by the runtime, and the JSON Pointer branch was unbounded in depth while the runtime stopped at sixteen (#72). tests/test_receipt_schema.py holds both bounds to those named constants and holds the contract and the runtime to the same accepted set at 127, 128, 129 and 160 characters and at sixteen and seventeen reference tokens; tools/pattern_gate.py rebuilds this pattern from the runtime vocabulary on every run, which checks the grammar and not the maxLength beside it. A pointer that carries any other word cannot enter an observation, so it cannot enter a receipt.

untrusted_envelope.$comment: Every field here is caller-declared and unauthenticated. The constants pin this artifact as unsigned: a later signing layer must publish a new schema version rather than relabel these documents.

deterministic_payload.$comment: Claim-minimal by construction: hashes, statuses, counts, structural pointers, and limitations only. No timestamp, signature, reviewer, run-environment, or semantic patient value may appear, and additionalProperties is false at every level so an added claim fails closed.

limitations.$comment: The mandated disclosure set, pinned in publication order (F-030, docs/09-TEST-AND-EVALUATION.md section 4), and closed exactly like the compiled-plan and compiled-pack limitation sets. A report template may not drop, reword, reorder, or pad these disclosures, and this is the only free-text-shaped field in the payload, so closing it keeps the payload hash-and-count minimal: changing the disclosures requires a new contract version.

prefixItems.const: Synthetic reference fixture only; not an approved clinical oracle.
A passing result does not establish safety, compliance, or certification.
Patient data is prohibited; bounded checks cannot prove an input is synthetic.
This iteration does not ingest FHIR or sign artifacts.

summary.$comment: One count per status in the published algebra; a status may not be silently dropped from or added to a receipt summary.

divergence.$comment: B-031, A-034. One entry per concept the case manifest declares, in the manifest's concept order, computed from the case and the observations alone: the rules do not reach it. pathway is the checkpoint order the comparison walked and is pinned so a reader of the payload need not know the runtime's order.

checkpoints.$comment: One state per checkpoint, in pathway order, so an unobserved boundary is visible as unobserved rather than absent from the list.

expected_sha256s.$comment: The sorted, distinct hashes of every value the case manifest declares for the concept: one for gender identity, name to use, and pronouns; as many as the manifest carries for recorded sex or gender and SPCU, possibly none. Carried for all five concepts whether or not any rule names the concept, and unsalted, like every other value hash in the payload: for a concept whose value space is small, such as pronouns, the hash of a declared value is recoverable by enumeration. A record-list concept is compared as its whole list, so an observation set that captures only some of the declared records at a boundary reads as diverged there, never as partial agreement.

value_sha256s.$comment: The sorted, distinct value hashes observed at this checkpoint; empty exactly when the state is unobserved, which the if/then below enforces.

from_expected.$comment: The first observed checkpoint whose value hashes are not the expected hashes. at is null exactly when the status is agreed_where_observed or unobserved, and the if/then below holds a hand-edited document to that: a located status with no location, or a location with an unlocated status, fails the contract rather than reaching a renderer.

from_previous.$comment: The first observed checkpoint whose value hashes differ from the previous observed checkpoint's. after is that previous observed checkpoint, so a divergence found across an unobserved gap is located between after and at, and the gap has no field to be named in. after is null when there was no earlier observed checkpoint, which only an indeterminate entry can say (a diverged entry needs two observed sides); both are null when the status is agreed_where_observed or unobserved. The allOf below holds a hand-edited document to those pairings.

outcome.$comment: Hashes stand in for every expected, observed, and source value; reason codes are a closed set so an unpublished reason cannot reach a receipt.

observed_sha256s.$comment: The sorted value hashes of every observation the predicate read at the outcome's checkpoint, or, for preserved_across, at both preserved_from and checkpoint with no marker of which hash came from which: the rule that rule_set_sha256 pins names both checkpoints, and a pass is exactly the case where the two hashes are one. No maxItems: the observation-set contract publishes no count bound, so record_count may legitimately carry as many hashes as the set holds at the checkpoint, and the 1 MiB input bound is what limits it.

reason.$comment: One affirmative and one failure reason per predicate in the rule-set 0.2 contract, plus the three evidence-state reasons. A pass may carry only an affirmative reason, a fail only a failure reason, and an indeterminate only missing_evidence or ambiguous_evidence; tests/test_property_invariants.py holds that partition.

trace.$comment: A-035. Where the outcome's evidence came from: the distinct source hash and structural pointer of every observation the predicate read, and the distinct version and hash of every mapping they came through, both sorted. A predicate that stops at an evidence gate carries the observations of the checkpoint that decided the verdict: for preserved_across with one side observed and the other missing or ambiguous, that is the failing side only, so the trace is empty when the failing side had no observation even though the other side had one. The assertion and its version are the outcome's rule_id and rule_version; the runner version is the payload's. Oracle and pack identity are not carried, because no governed oracle or pack exists to name (B-010, B-029, B-030).
